Analysts project their own cash flows. How the scenarios are built: growth moves by the gap between the analysts’ consensus and their lowest and highest revenue forecasts (24 analysts): −2.0 and +2.3 points (between 2 and 8); the discount rate 1 point higher or lower; long-term growth 0.5 points lower or higher. The starting cash flow is the same in all three.

With your assumptions the shares trade 68% above your estimated value. The price assumes more than your inputs. To justify today’s price with your discount rate, free cash flow would have to grow about 33.3% a year for five years (reverse DCF).

Why is my value so far from the price?
Analysts project their own cash flows. Instead of starting from last year’s free cash flow and one growth rate, they model each year from their revenue and margin forecasts, so a business coming out of a weak year (or a cyclical one, like semiconductors) gets a higher starting point than the past shows.
The analysts’ consensus target (5 analysts) is 410.00, 64% above the price. With your other inputs unchanged, reaching it would need a discount rate of about 4.1% or growth of about 43.0% a year for five years. That rate is below what analysts normally use, so most of the gap is presumably in the cash flows they expect: with your discount rate and growth rates, the target implies a starting free cash flow of about $2.8B, 4.5× the figure you are using. We do not see the analysts’ models: this is inferred from their target, which can also lag a recent fall in the price.
None of these makes your number wrong: it is what your assumptions say. The useful question is which assumption you believe, and the sensitivity table below shows how much each one matters.

Like other concession and infrastructure groups, most of its debt is project finance: each concession borrows on its own and repays from its own cash flows, without recourse to the parent. Profits are far above their own history (net profit $1.3B against a typical $95M in previous years). In a cyclical business the starting point decides almost everything: from last year’s free cash flow ($2.4B) the value is 93.22; from the 3-year average ($2.0B) it is 77.01. Why is my value so far from the price?
Your discount rate is high (13.2%). It comes from a beta of 2.34 (already adjusted towards 1 from a raw 3): over the last five years the share has moved much more than the market. That is a fair measure of risk for a cyclical business, but it weighs heavily on the result; each point less in the discount rate raises the value a lot (see the sensitivity table).
Analysts project their own cash flows. Instead of starting from last year’s free cash flow and one growth rate, they model each year from their revenue and margin forecasts, so a business coming out of a weak year (or a cyclical one, like semiconductors) gets a higher starting point than the past shows.
The analysts’ consensus target (17 analysts) is 206.50, 53% above the price. With your other inputs unchanged, reaching it would need a discount rate of about 6.2% or growth of about 22.8% a year for five years. That rate is below what analysts normally use, so most of the gap is presumably in the cash flows they expect: with your discount rate and growth rates, the target implies a starting free cash flow of about $5.6B, 2.9× the figure you are using. We do not see the analysts’ models: this is inferred from their target, which can also lag a recent fall in the price.

Why is my value so far from the price?
Analysts project their own cash flows. Instead of starting from last year’s free cash flow and one growth rate, they model each year from their revenue and margin forecasts, so a business coming out of a weak year (or a cyclical one, like semiconductors) gets a higher starting point than the past shows.

That is a fair measure of risk for a cyclical business, but it weighs heavily on the result; each point less in the discount rate raises the value a lot (see the sensitivity table).
Analysts project their own cash flows. Instead of starting from last year’s free cash flow and one growth rate, they model each year from their revenue and margin forecasts, so a business coming out of a weak year (or a cyclical one, like semiconductors) gets a higher starting point than the past shows.

How the scenarios are built: growth moves by the gap between the analysts’ consensus and their lowest and highest revenue forecasts (5 analysts): −2.0 and +2.0 points (between 2 and 8); the discount rate 1 point higher or lower; long-term growth 0.5 points lower or higher. With your assumptions the shares trade 45% below your estimated value: a wide margin of safety. To justify today’s price with your discount rate, free cash flow could shrink about 5.0% a year for five years (reverse DCF).

Why is my value so far from the price?
Analysts project their own cash flows. Instead of starting from last year’s free cash flow and one growth rate, they model each year from their revenue and margin forecasts, so a business coming out of a weak year (or a cyclical one, like semiconductors) gets a higher starting point than the past shows.

Why is my value so far from the price?
Analysts project their own cash flows. Instead of starting from last year’s free cash flow and one growth rate, they model each year from their revenue and margin forecasts, so a business coming out of a weak year (or a cyclical one, like semiconductors) gets a higher starting point than the past shows.
